idiom_name: explicit parameter/prop relay plus one grouped context object
implementation_notes: Language-neutral form: keep the relay explicit by default - the dependency is a prop or parameter on every layer between owner and consumer - and treat a layer that forwards a value it never reads as the smell. Before reaching for an ambient mechanism, try the structural fixes: move the state down to the nearest common ancestor of its consumers (state colocation), inline the pass-through layer, or pass the consumer itself (children/elements) instead of the data. When the chain genuinely has to stay deep and wide, group the relayed values into one small immutable context object (app context struct, request scope) and offer it through the platform's scoped mechanism - framework context, scoped value, implicit parameter, task-local value, DI scope - rather than through five individual parameters. Keep the provider scope as tight as possible and never hide data a consumer requires in ambient state.
code_sketch:
owner -> relay (does not read) -> relay (does not read) -> consumer

# fix 1 - move the state to the consumers' nearest common ancestor (state colocation)
# fix 2 - pass the consumer itself down instead of the data it needs (composition)
# fix 3 - bind one immutable context object at a scope boundary:
with scope(user=current_user):      # scoped value / provider / implicit / task-local
    render_tree()                   # consumers read their dependency directly
pitfalls: Declaring the relay in a signature and then reading it inside the intermediate recreates the coupling the decision is meant to remove.
A single shared mutable context passed everywhere becomes a god object: every layer can reach every value, and ownership disappears.
Adding a provider for every value turns explicit props into ambient globals; the provider scope must stay as narrow as the consumers' common ancestor.
Wrong move: replace a two-level React prop with context -> reuse fails because the dependency is hidden behind provider placement -> instead pass the prop or compose the consumer.

Wrong move: use Vue provide/inject for a local parent-child contract -> API clarity fails because the dependency disappears from the child signature and missing providers warn at runtime -> instead keep local data in props.

Wrong move: call a Svelte context getter outside its provider subtree -> isolation fails because createContext's getter throws without a parent set -> instead keep the context boundary explicit or pass the value as a prop to isolated leaves.
